page: Amazon Web Services i7i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are supplemented by 320 MB of shared L3 cache, full support for AVX-512, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The hardware allocation pairs these cores with 512 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU memory density.

Storage and throughput are key characteristics of the i7i.16xlarge profile. The server includes 15,000 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrated 287.15 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, while static web serving throughput reached 106.15 GB/sec. CPU benchmarks placed the instance in the upper tiers, scoring 21,127 in multi-core Geekbench and 78,637.66 in PassMark CPU tests, reflecting stable compute capacity across all threads.

The presence of 15 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage combined with high memory bandwidth delivers strong performance density for I/O-intensive architectures without relying on remote network-attached disks. Benchmark results confirm elevated throughput in transactional workloads, including 87.75 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database operation scores. However, with zero GPUs present, parallel accelerator-bound compute tasks are restricted to CPU-based AVX-512 or AMX operations.

The hardware configuration suits high-concurrency transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, massive in-memory caching layers, search index clusters, and large-scale ETL pipelines requiring immediate low-latency disk access.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized cloud instance powered by a 32-core, 64-thread Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 512 GB of DDR5 system memory at 6 GHz, along with 15,000 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a 38 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, the configuration delivered 287.15 GB/sec uncached large-block memory read bandwidth, a PassMark database score in the top ten percent, and 87.75 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware support includes AVX-512 and Intel AMX extensions, though the platform features no discrete GPUs. This combination of dense local NVMe disk capacity, broad memory bandwidth, and 64 dedicated compute threads makes the i7i.16xlarge well aligned with heavy relational database workloads, large distributed cache nodes, search indexing services, and low-latency data ingestion clusters.
